newsitem.title: USA: Delay in China joining WTO hurts world trade - Dai.
newsitem.headline: Delay in China joining WTO hurts world trade - Dai.

text.p: In a clear reference to the U.S., China on Tuesday said the delay by "certain parties' in letting it join the World Trade Organisation (WTO) was hurting the development of world trade.
Washington is pressing its fifth largest trade partner to open up its markets to imports as a condition of its membership of the trade body.

"The unreasonable demands of certain contracting parties have delayed China's accession to the WTO...bringing unfavourable consequences for the healthy development of world trade,' head of the People's Bank of China, Dai Xianglong told the annual meeting of the IMF and World Bank.
He critcised the frequent use of trade sanctions by some industrial countries and said it was vital for them to reduce non-trade barriers and give greater access to developing countries.
China had already said it was prepared to take on the obligations of membership, Dai added.
He also urged Western nations to improve their economic peformance.

"The protracted high fiscal deficits and their excessive reliance on monetary policy have not only been unfavourable to their domestic economic growth, but have also been a major factor underlying the international financial market instability," he said.

Industrial nations should strengthen their budgetary positions, push ahead with labour market reform and so create favourable conditions for lower interest rates and minimise uncertainty in the world economy, he added.

Pointing to the Chinese economy, he said he was well aware of the challenges it faced, especially in making state firms more efficient, further strengthening its own fiscal postion and improving the quality of commercial bank loans.
"The solution to these problems lies in deepening the reform and maintaining appropriately tight monetary and fiscal policies,' Dai said.
